parole.testo: Derived from Finnic, perhaps with an original meaning of “distant or high land”; compare to Karelian edäh (“far away”) + Karelian mua (“land”).

parole.significato: kaluga, great Siberian sturgeon (type of sturgeon: Huso dauricus)
parole.testo: Probably of Finnic origin (cf. Finnish kala (“fish”)).

parole.significato: to hobble, to dodder, to toddle, to stump
parole.testo: Unknown, perhaps a Finnic borrowing, compare Finnish kävellä (“to walk”), or a slangy term from Northwest Semitic related to Classical Syriac ܟܒܠܐ (kaḇlā, keḇlā, “clog, fetter”). Cognate with Serbo-Croatian kovìtlati.

parole.significato: smelt (a fish from the Osmeridae family; most commonly, of species Osmerus eperlanus)
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Finnic language; compare to Finnish kuore, Karelian kuoreh, Veps koreh, Livvi kuorʹoi.
From a Finnic language, compare Veps lohi, Finnish lohi, Estonian lõhe.
Borrowed from some Finnic source; compare Finnish muurain (“cloudberry”).

Borrowed from a Finnic language, from Proto-Finnic *purku.
Borrowed from a Finnic language, from Proto-Finnic *salakka.
Borrowed from a Finnic language; compare to Finnish harjus, Estonian harjus.

parole.significato: a kind of pastry likened to a vatrushka but unsweet and often filled with potato
parole.testo: Borrowed from Finnic, compare Karelian šanki (“harvested cereals; stubble”); Komi-Zyrian, Udmurt and Eastern Mari have the word for the pastry from Russian.
Borrowed from Estonian mõis or from a related Finnic language (cf. Finnish moisio, Livonian mȯizõ, Votic mõizõ).
